answers.question: How does this simplification compare with existing methods of simplifying logic?
answers.answer: It ties. Across 6 circuits and 3 seeds (18 results) the evolved and hand-designed netlists mapped to identical LUT counts and identical depth under one identical abc -lut 6 recipe: 0 wins, 18 ties, 0 losses.

reproduce.behavior: Renders deterministic playback of a preserved receipt. It runs no benchmark, no test suite, no synthesis, and no cracking run.
reproduce.workspacePathConstraint: The tape records to an absolute path under /Volumes/Code/MuleinLabs and must be adjusted if the workspace is relocated.

capturedAtBasis: Rendered during this documentation pass; the underlying experiment predates it and is dated in the receipt itself

captureMethod.mode: normal-speed playback of a preserved receipt

artifacts.kind: durable byte-for-byte copy used by the tape

experiment.identicalFlowBothSides: read LUT6 model + emitted candidate; hierarchy -check; proc; flatten; opt; techmap; opt; abc -lut 6; opt_clean; check -assert; write_json
experiment.proof: miter -equiv -flatten; sat -prove trigger 0 against independent behavioural RTL

timingContext.interpretation: The capture replays preserved text at normal speed. Any elapsed-time figures visible on screen are historical observations from the original run on one Apple-silicon host, not fresh measurements and not portable performance contracts.

claimBoundaries: This is playback of a preserved receipt. Nothing was re-run for the capture.
The measured outcome is a null: no retained finalist beat or lost to its identically mapped baseline.
Pre-mapping LUT reductions are real but are not a simplification win, because ABC removes the same redundancy.
LUT6 count and LUT-level depth under one ABC flow are implementation proxies only.
Nothing here establishes physical area, delay, frequency, power, or any general advantage over ABC.
The 8-bit adder search was sampled at 512 of 65,536 rows; every mapped finalist was still SAT-proved over the full input space.
Six small fixtures on one host. No claim follows for arbitrary topologies or industrial designs.
